title: Exact restriction to a stack test fibre preserves injective modules
statement:
Work in the universes and small-skeleton convention of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $h:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of algebraic stacks over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], and let $y\in\mathcal Y(V)$ be an object over an $S$-scheme $V$. Categories fibred in groupoids and their $2$-fibre products have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Give these categories their inherited big fppf sites and structure sheaves [def-sfb-stack-quasi-coherent-algebra], or their big etale sites with the same objects, arrows and structure sheaves and coverings lying over jointly surjective etale scheme families [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Fix $\tau\in\{\mathrm{et},\mathrm{fppf}\}$, put $\mathcal X_y=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}(\mathit{Sch}/V)$, and write $p_y:\mathcal X_y\to\mathcal X$ for the projection. Precomposition, with its original restriction maps, defines an exact additive functor on all structure-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]
$$p_y^{-1}:\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal X_\tau,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})\longrightarrow\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal X_{y,\tau},\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_y}).$$
On an object $(x,T\to V,\alpha)$ over $T$ it has value $M(x)$ with the original $\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$-action; in particular $p_y^{-1}\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_y}$. If $I$ is injective in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal X_\tau,\mathcal O_{\mathcal X})$ [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then $p_y^{-1}I$ is injective in $\operatorname{Mod}(\mathcal X_{y,\tau},\mathcal O_{\mathcal X_y})$. No representability, quasi-compactness, quasi-separatedness or flatness is assumed for $h$, and no quasi-coherence condition is imposed on the modules.

source.place: Tag 06X2 (lemma-pullback-injective-modules), specialized to the test-fibre projection; Tag 06WY (lemma-fibre-products), equalizers for algebraic stacks; Tag 06TS (lemma-functoriality-sheaves), exact inverse image by precomposition. This is the injective-preservation input used in the proof of lemma-pushforward-restriction.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C=\mathcal X_y$ and $u=p_y$. The fibrewise triple construction of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] makes $\mathcal C$ fibred in groupoids: pull back the object $x$, the map to $V$, and the isomorphism $\alpha$ along the same base arrow. Its lifting uniqueness follows componentwise. Both total categories are small in the stipulated universe. Thus [lem-sfb-fibred-site-functor-continuity], with the base scheme site in the chosen topology $\tau$, makes $u$ continuous and cocontinuous. It applies for both topologies because their coverings are exactly the inherited scheme coverings. Since $u$ leaves the underlying scheme and base arrow unchanged, $R=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ satisfies $R\circ u=\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$ as ring sheaves, including restriction maps. Apply [lem-trf-ringed-site-restriction-generator-data] to obtain an additive exact restriction functor $T$ on all module sheaves. Its formula on $(x,v,\alpha)$ is $TM(x,v,\alpha)=M(x)$ with its original action and restrictions, so this is the functor and the structure-ring equality asserted in the statement.

source.place: Tag 06TS, lemma-functoriality-sheaves; section-modules, precomposition and unchanged structure ring

proof.text: The functor $u$ is faithful. Indeed an arrow of triples consists of an arrow $a:x\to x'$ and an arrow of $\mathit{Sch}/V$ with the same base scheme map, satisfying the compatibility with $\alpha,\alpha'$. For fixed $a$ that second arrow is unique, so two parallel arrows with the same image in $\mathcal X$ coincide. This uses no faithfulness assumption on $h$.

source.place: Tag 06X2 hypotheses; fibrewise description of the test-fibre projection

proof.text: Both total categories have fibre products: for arrows to a common object lift the underlying scheme fibre product of [def-pc-fibre-product]; [lem-sfb-cartesian-lift-pullback-square] gives its universal property because every arrow is cartesian. Applying $u$ leaves this base square unchanged and still gives cartesian arrows, so its image is again a pullback by the same lemma. Thus $u$ preserves fibre products.

For parallel arrows $A,B:z\to z'$ in $\mathcal C$, write $z=(x,v,\alpha)$. By [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-total-equalizers], let $e:w\to x$ equalize $u(A),u(B)$ in $\mathcal X$, and let $t:W\to T$ be its base map. The triple $\widetilde w=(w,v t,t^*\alpha)$ uses the canonical cartesian identifications $h(w)\simeq t^*h(x)$; it has a canonical arrow $\widetilde e:\widetilde w\to z$ above $e$. Faithfulness makes $A\widetilde e=B\widetilde e$. Any equalizing arrow $k:z''\to z$ has a unique factorization $u(k)=e l$ in $\mathcal X$. This $l$ lifts to a morphism $z''\to\widetilde w$: its map to $V$ is forced by $v''=v\,p(k)=v t\,p(l)$, and its isomorphism compatibility is exactly that of $k$ after the cartesian identifications. Faithfulness gives uniqueness. Hence $\widetilde e$ is an equalizer and $u$ preserves it.

source.place: Tag 06WY (3), lemma-fibre-products; Tag 06WZ (2), lemma-fibre-products-morphism, with the test-fibre lifting written out

proof.text: For $z$ over $T$, apply [lem-sfb-fibred-test-object-ringed-localization] to the categories fibred in groupoids $\mathcal C$ and $\mathcal X$ in the chosen topology $\tau$: the functors $p_z:\mathcal C/z\to\mathit{Sch}/T$ and $p_{u(z)}:\mathcal X/u(z)\to\mathit{Sch}/T$, sending an arrow into the distinguished object to its underlying scheme map, are equivalences of ringed sites for the localized topologies and the restricted structure sheaves, and both identify the ring on an object over $W$ with $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$. Since $u$ is a functor over $\mathit{Sch}/S$ that leaves underlying scheme maps unchanged, the induced slice functor $u_z:\mathcal C/z\to\mathcal X/u(z)$ satisfies $p_{u(z)}\circ u_z=p_z$ strictly. Hence $u_z$ is an equivalence of categories (two out of three), and a family in $\mathcal C/z$ covers if and only if its image in $\mathit{Sch}/T$ is a $\tau$-covering, if and only if its image under $u_z$ covers. The ring sheaves $\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}|_z$ and $\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}|_{u(z)}\circ u_z$ both take the value $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ with the same pullbacks, as already noted in step 1. Thus $u_z$ is an equivalence of ringed slice sites.

source.place: Tag 06W9, lemma-localizing-structure-sheaf (via lem-sfb-fibred-test-object-ringed-localization); proof of Tag 06X2, equivalence of localized ringed sites

proof.text: Steps 1, 3, 4 and 5 verify every hypothesis of [lem-sfb-ringed-site-slice-equivalence-exact-shriek] for $u$, $R=\mathcal O_{\mathcal X}$ and $R'=\mathcal O_{\mathcal C}$. Obtain an exact additive $L\dashv T$. In particular $L$ preserves monomorphisms. Apply [lem-exc-rg-right-adjoint-preserves-injectives] to this adjunction: for each injective module $I$ on $\mathcal X$, the module $TI$ on $\mathcal C$ is injective. Concretely a map $M\to TI$ along a monomorphism $M\hookrightarrow N$ transposes to $LM\to I$; extend it across the monomorphism $LM\hookrightarrow LN$ and transpose back. Together with step 1 this proves all clauses, for arbitrary $h$ and arbitrary module sheaves.
